title: `createLazyPlugin`'s own JSDoc teaches a call that does not compile — `import('@object-ui/plugin-grid')` has no `default` export
body:
Found while clearing `content/docs/guide/deployment.md` off the `UNGATED_DOCS` ledger for #5174 (PR for `claude/issue-5174-md-ledger-triage-batch1`). Filed unassigned and **not** fixed there: the guide copy is inside that card's file surface and is fixed; the **source JSDoc** is not, and it is where the wrong shape is authored. ## What `packages/react/src/LazyPluginLoader.tsx:123` declares: ```ts export function createLazyPlugin

( importFn: () => Promise<{ default: React.ComponentType

}>, options?: LazyPluginOptions ): React.ComponentType

``` Its own `@example` block, three times over (`:98`, `:103`, `:109`, carried through to `packages/react/dist/LazyPluginLoader.d.ts:40/45/51`), passes: ```tsx const ObjectGrid = createLazyPlugin( () => import('@object-ui/plugin-grid') ); ``` `@object-ui/plugin-grid` has **no default export**. `packages/plugin-grid/dist/index.d.ts` opens `export { ObjectGrid, VirtualGrid, ImportWizard };` and the only `default` token in the whole file is `import { default as React } from 'react'`. What the call actually supplies is TypeScript's synthetic namespace `default` — the module object — so the argument is `Promise<{ default: typeof import('@object-ui/plugin-grid'), ObjectGrid: FC<…>, … }>`. ## Measured Compiled against the built `dist/` by `scripts/check-doc-snippet-types.mjs` (the same harness, same `--strict` program): ``` TS2322: Type 'Promise<{ default: typeof import(".../packages/plugin-grid/dist/index"); ObjectGrid: FC; … }>' is not assignable to type 'Promise<{ default: ComponentType; }>'. Type 'typeof import(".../packages/plugin-grid/dist/index")' is not assignable to type 'ComponentType'. ``` This is not only a type error. At runtime `React.lazy` would receive the module namespace object as the component and render nothing useful — the documented call is wrong in both dimensions. ## The shape that does compile Verified green in the same program, and this is what the guide now says: ```tsx const ObjectGrid = createLazyPlugin( // The plugin package has no default export — name the component you want. async () => ({ default: (await import('@object-ui/plugin-grid')).ObjectGrid }), { fallback:

Loading grid...
} ); ``` Note the `async` form specifically: the `.then((m) => ({ default: m.ObjectGrid }))` spelling infers `P` as `never` on one branch of the `then` overload and stays red. ## Why this is filed rather than folded in ⛔ **Do not "fix" this by adding a default export to `@object-ui/plugin-grid`.** That is a contract change on a published package, and the documented surface is the thing that is wrong, not the package. Two candidate shapes for whoever picks this up, and they are not the same decision: 1. **Correct the three JSDoc examples in place** (cheapest, matches what the guide now teaches). 2. **Tighten `importFn`'s parameter type** so a namespace object cannot satisfy it silently — worth checking whether any in-repo caller currently relies on the loose shape before proposing it. ## Reachability `packages/react`'s README is already covered by `check-doc-snippet-types`, but a JSDoc `@example` inside a `.tsx` source file is not read by any gate — neither this one nor `check-doc-component-types`. So the wrong call survives in the published `.d.ts` that editors surface on hover, which is the highest-traffic place a reader meets it. Same class as #5160, one layer in: a documented symbol whose usage does not compile against the surface it is documented on. Related: #5174 (the ledger card that surfaced it), #5160, #5053.
